    @staticmethod
    def get_adj(nodes: List[int], edges: List[Tuple[int, int]]) -> Dict[int, Set[int]]:
        """Builds an adjacency list representation of the graph."""
        adj = collections.defaultdict(set)
        for u, v in edges:
            adj[u].add(v)
            adj[v].add(u)
        # Ensure all nodes are keys in the adjacency list, even isolated ones
        for node in nodes:
            if node not in adj:
                 adj[node] = set()
        return adj

    @staticmethod
    def get_complement_adj(nodes: List[int], adj: Dict[int, Set[int]]) -> Dict[int, Set[int]]:
        """Builds the adjacency list of the complement graph."""
        adj_comp = collections.defaultdict(set)
        node_set = set(nodes)
        for u in nodes:
            # Neighbors in the original graph
            neighbors = adj.get(u, set())
            # Non-neighbors in the original graph (excluding self)
            non_neighbors = node_set - neighbors - {u}
            # These non-neighbors become neighbors in the complement graph
            adj_comp[u] = non_neighbors
        # Ensure all nodes are keys in the complement adjacency list
        for node in nodes:

                  # This handles nodes that might not have been keys in the original adj
                  # (e.g., completely isolated nodes, or if adj was built sparsely)
                  # An isolated node in G is connected to all others in G_comp.
                  adj_comp[node] = node_set - {node}
        return adj_comp

    @staticmethod
    def _find_cliques_recursive(potential_clique: Set[int], 
                                candidates: Set[int], 
                                excluded: Set[int], 
                                graph_adj: Dict[int, Set[int]], 
                                maximal_cliques_list: List[Set[int]]):
        """Recursive helper for Bron-Kerbosch algorithm with pivoting to find maximal cliques."""
        
        # Base case: If P (candidates) and X (excluded) are empty, R (potential_clique) is a maximal clique
        if not candidates and not excluded:
            maximal_cliques_list.append(potential_clique) 
            return

        # Pruning: If P is empty, no more candidates can be added to extend the clique from this path
        if not candidates:
             return

        # Pivot selection: Choose pivot 'u' from P union X 
        # that maximizes the number of neighbors currently in P. This helps prune the search.
        pivot_candidates = candidates | excluded
        # If pivot_candidates is somehow empty here, something is wrong, but return to be safe
        if not pivot_candidates:

        pivot = max(pivot_candidates, key=lambda u: len(candidates.intersection(graph_adj.get(u, set()))))
        
        # Iterate through candidate nodes 'q' that are NOT neighbors of the pivot.

        candidates_without_pivot_neighbors = list(candidates - graph_adj.get(pivot, set()))

            neighbors_of_q = graph_adj.get(q, set())
            # Recursive call: Explore extending the clique with 'q'
            MaxMaximalCocktailsCustomStrategy._find_cliques_recursive(

                candidates.intersection(neighbors_of_q), # New candidates: common neighbors of R U {q}
                excluded.intersection(neighbors_of_q), # New excluded: common neighbors already processed

            candidates.remove(q)

    """
    Calculates all Maximal Independent Sets (MIS) of a graph.
    Uses Bron-Kerbosch algorithm on the complement graph.

    for node in node_set:
        adj[node] = set()
    # Populate edges, ensuring nodes are valid

            adj[u].add(v)
            adj[v].add(u)

    # Build adjacency list for the complement graph G_bar
    comp_adj = collections.defaultdict(set)

        non_neighbors = node_set - neighbors_in_g - {u}
        comp_adj[u] = non_neighbors

    def find_cliques_recursive(potential_clique: Set[int], candidates: Set[int], excluded: Set[int]):

        nonlocal mis_list_sets
        
        # Base case: If P and X are empty, R is a maximal clique
        if not candidates and not excluded:
            if potential_clique: # Avoid adding empty set if graph is empty
                 mis_list_sets.add(frozenset(potential_clique))
            return

            nonlocal cliques
            # Base case: If P and X are empty, R is a maximal clique

    def _find_cliques_recursive(self, graph_adj: Dict[int, List[int]], potential_clique: set[int], candidates: set[int], excluded: set[int], cliques_list: List[List[int]]):
        """Recursive step of the Bron-Kerbosch algorithm with pivoting."""
        # Base case: Found a maximal clique
        if not candidates and not excluded:
            # Add a copy of the found clique
            cliques_list.append(list(potential_clique))
            return

        # Pruning condition: If candidates is empty, cannot extend further
        if not candidates:
            return

        # Pivot selection: Choose pivot u from candidates union excluded
        # This optimizes by reducing recursive calls.
        pivot_candidates = candidates | excluded
        # The key function calculates the size of the intersection between neighbors of u and candidates
        pivot = max(pivot_candidates, key=lambda u: len(set(graph_adj.get(u, [])) & candidates))

        pivot_neighbors = set(graph_adj.get(pivot, []))
        # Iterate through nodes in P \ N(pivot) (candidates without pivot's neighbors)
        # Iterating over a copy is crucial because 'candidates' is modified during the loop
        candidates_to_iterate = list(candidates - pivot_neighbors)

        for q in candidates_to_iterate:
            neighbors_of_q = set(graph_adj.get(q, []))
            # Recursive call for the subgraph induced by neighbors of q
            self._find_cliques_recursive(
                graph_adj,
                potential_clique | {q},          # Add q to the potential clique
                candidates & neighbors_of_q,     # New candidates are common neighbors of q and old candidates
                excluded & neighbors_of_q,       # New excluded are common neighbors of q and old excluded
                cliques_list
            )
            # Backtrack: Remove q from candidates and add it to excluded

            excluded.add(q)

    def _build_adj(self, nodes: List[int], edges: List[Tuple[int, int]]) -> Dict[int, Set[int]]:
        """Builds an adjacency list representation (dict mapping node to set of neighbors)."""
        adj = collections.defaultdict(set)
        for u, v in edges:
            adj[u].add(v)
            adj[v].add(u)
        # Ensure all nodes are keys, even isolated ones
        for node in nodes:
            if node not in adj:
                adj[node] = set()
        return adj

    def _build_complement_adj(self, nodes: List[int], edges: List[Tuple[int, int]]) -> Dict[int, Set[int]]:
        """Builds the adjacency list for the complement graph."""
        complement_adj = collections.defaultdict(set)
        nodes_set = set(nodes)
        original_adj = self._build_adj(nodes, edges)

        for u in nodes:
            # Neighbors in complement are non-neighbors in original (excluding self)
            non_neighbors = nodes_set - original_adj.get(u, set()) - {u}
            complement_adj[u] = non_neighbors
        return complement_adj

    def _find_maximal_cliques_recursive(self,
                                         potential_clique: Set[int],
                                         candidates: Set[int],
                                         excluded: Set[int],
                                         complement_adj: Dict[int, Set[int]],
                                         cliques_list: List[List[int]]):
        """Recursive step of the Bron-Kerbosch algorithm with pivoting."""
        
        # Base case: If no candidates can extend the clique and none were excluded that could, it's maximal.
        if not candidates and not excluded:
            # Found a maximal clique
            cliques_list.append(sorted(list(potential_clique))) # Store sorted list
            return

        # Pruning: If no candidates left, backtrack.
        if not candidates:
             return

        # Pivot Selection: Choose a pivot 'u' from candidates union excluded.
        # Heuristic: choose 'u' maximizing |candidates intersect neighbors(u)|.
        pivot_candidates_pool = candidates | excluded
        pivot = max(pivot_candidates_pool, key=lambda u: len(candidates & complement_adj.get(u, set())), default=None)

        # Use .get(pivot, set()) to handle cases where pivot might somehow not be in adj keys (though unlikely)
        candidates_to_iterate = list(candidates - complement_adj.get(pivot, set()))

            node_neighbors = complement_adj.get(node, set())
            # Recursive call for the node added to the potential clique
            self._find_maximal_cliques_recursive(

    # Base case: no nodes means no MIS

        self.history = self._model.history
        self.strategy_type = StrategyType.SMT
        self._clique_list_internal: List[Set[int]] = [] # Instance variable for BK results

    def update_model_field(self, field_name: str, value: Any):
        if hasattr(self._model, field_name):
            setattr(self._model, field_name, value)

    def _find_cliques_bk_recursive(self, potential_clique: Set[int], candidates: Set[int], excluded: Set[int], graph_adj: Dict[int, Set[int]]):
        """
        Recursive helper for Bron-Kerbosch algorithm with pivoting.
        Finds maximal cliques in the graph defined by graph_adj.
        Results are stored in self._clique_list_internal.
        """
        if not candidates and not excluded:
            # Base case: Found a maximal clique
            if potential_clique: # Ensure we don't add empty set if graph was empty initially
                self._clique_list_internal.append(potential_clique.copy())
            return

        if not candidates:
            return # Cannot extend further

        # Pivot selection: Choose u in P U X maximizing |P intersect N(u)|
        # Use a list comprehension and max for clarity and correctness
        pivot_candidates = candidates | excluded
        pivot = -1
        max_neighbors_in_candidates = -1

        # Find the best pivot node
        best_pivot = -1
        max_intersect_size = -1
        for u in pivot_candidates:
            neighbors = graph_adj.get(u, set())
            intersect_size = len(candidates & neighbors)
            if intersect_size > max_intersect_size:
                max_intersect_size = intersect_size
                best_pivot = u
        
        # If no pivot found (e.g., candidates exist but no edges among them in pivot_candidates), pick one from candidates
        if best_pivot == -1:
            if candidates: # Ensure candidates is not empty before using next(iter(...))
                 best_pivot = next(iter(candidates))
            else:
                 # This case should not be reached if 'if not candidates:' check above works
                 return 

        pivot_neighbors = graph_adj.get(best_pivot, set())
        # Iterate over candidates not adjacent to the pivot: P \ N(pivot)
        # Important: Iterate over a copy of the set to allow modification during iteration
        extensible_candidates = list(candidates - pivot_neighbors)

        for q in extensible_candidates:
            neighbors_of_q = graph_adj.get(q, set())
            # Recursive call
            self._find_cliques_bk_recursive(potential_clique | {q},
                                           candidates & neighbors_of_q,
                                           excluded & neighbors_of_q,
                                           graph_adj)
            # Backtrack: Move q from candidates to excluded
            candidates.remove(q)
            excluded.add(q)

        for u, v in edges:
            if u in nodes_set and v in nodes_set:
                adj[u].add(v)
                adj[v].add(u)

        adj_comp = {node: set() for node in nodes_set}
        for u in nodes_set:
            neighbors_in_G = adj.get(u, set())
            # Non-neighbors are nodes in nodes_set - {u} - neighbors_in_G

                final_edge_to_return = tuple(sorted((nodes_list[0], nodes_list[1])))
            else:
                # Fallback 3: Graph has < 2 nodes. Cannot form an edge.
                final_edge_to_return = (-1, -1) # Indicate impossibility/error

        # Construct the response message
        return Info(
            sender=self.__class__.__name__,
            receiver=message.sender,
            difficulty=message.difficulty,
            message=[BaseMessageDataType(data=final_edge_to_return, type='custom')]
        )
"
